--- title: "Introduction to Quarto — Lab" subtitle: "RaukR 2026 · Day 1" author: "" date: "" --- ::: {.callout-note} ## Scope Build one penguins document with the authoring extras, then **cite it** and render it as a **branded Typst PDF**. Two challenges, one document: each is its own hands-on part, with a break between them. This is your **manuscript / team-project path**, the same route from an analysis to a submittable write-up. Everything runs on **base-R `datasets::penguins`** (R ≥ 4.5), so there's no data to download. **Before you start:** run through the **[Setup page](../../setup.qmd)** if you haven't. Its `00-check-setup.R` confirms R, Quarto, and the packages this lab uses. ::: ::: {.callout-tip appearance="simple"} You are working in the **`day1-intro/`** folder from the exercises download (open `day1-intro.Rproj`). See the [Setup page](../../setup.qmd#get-the-materials). Everything you render lands right next to your files. ::: Start every document with this setup (the challenges below assume it): ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} library(dplyr) library(ggplot2) library(gt) library(ggokabeito) # color-blind-safe (Okabe-Ito) scale -- see the Accessibility box data(penguins) penguins <- penguins |> filter(!is.na(bill_len), !is.na(bill_dep)) ``` ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Coming from R Markdown? (optional, 2-minute aside) You do **not** need to convert anything to work natively in Quarto. Start with `.qmd` directly. But if you have an `.Rmd` you want to bring over: - it renders **as-is** — Quarto reads `.Rmd` too; - cell options move from the chunk header to the `#|` "hash-pipe" (one YAML option per line); - `knitr::convert_chunk_header("doc.Rmd", output = "doc.qmd")` does the mechanical part. That's the whole migration. The rest of this lab is native `.qmd`. ::: ## Authoring Challenge > **Goal:** a penguins report with a cross-referenced **figure**, a cross-referenced **table**, a > **margin** element, and a display **equation**, rendered to HTML. ::: {.callout-note icon=false} ## {{< fa clipboard-list >}} Tasks 1. Create `my-report.qmd` **inside your open `day1-intro/` folder** (next to `references.bib` / `apa.csl`, so Part 2's paths and branding resolve later) with `format: html` and the setup cell at the top of this page. 2. Add a scatter plot of `bill_len` versus `bill_dep` colored by `species`. Give its cell `#| label: fig-bill` and a `#| fig-cap:`, then refer to it with `@fig-bill` **in the prose, outside the cell**. 3. Add a summary table. The `gt` plumbing is below. Your job is the **cross-reference mechanic**: give the cell `#| label: tbl-summary` and a `#| tbl-cap:`, then refer to it with `@tbl-summary`. ```r penguins |> summarise(bill_len = mean(bill_len), bill_dep = mean(bill_dep), .by = species) |> gt() ``` 4. Put the species counts in the **margin** with the cell option `#| column: margin`. 5. *(stretch)* Add the bill-shape ratio as a display equation, referenced with `@eq-ratio`. **Escape the underscores**: inside `$$…$$`, `bill_len` may render as a subscript (depending on the math renderer), so write: ```markdown $$ \text{ratio} = \frac{\text{bill\_len}}{\text{bill\_dep}} $$ {#eq-ratio} ``` 6. Render to HTML (`quarto render my-report.qmd`, or the editor's Render/Preview). ::: ::: {.callout-tip icon=false} ## {{< fa universal-access >}} Make it accessible The worked report does all three. Do the same in yours: - add a `#| fig-alt:` to every figure; - add `scale_color_okabe_ito()` (from `ggokabeito`) to your plot, keeping `shape = species`; - add `axe: {output: document}` under `format: html`, re-preview, and a WCAG report appears on the page (drop it again before you publish). See [Quarto's accessibility docs](https://quarto.org/docs/output-formats/html-accessibility.html). ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false} ## {{< fa circle-check >}} You should see A numbered **Figure 1** (the bill scatter, three separate clusters), a numbered **Table 1**, the counts sitting in the right margin, and an **Equation 1**, with `@fig-bill` / `@tbl-summary` / `@eq-ratio` rendering as live "Figure 1" / "Table 1" / "Equation 1" links. Your finished figure looks like this: ::: ::: {.cell} ::: {.cell-output-display} ![Target: bill length versus depth by species.](index_files/figure-html/fig-target-1.png){#fig-target fig-alt='Scatter plot of bill depth against bill length for three penguin species in distinct colors; the species form largely separate clusters.' width=576} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint - A cell becomes a cross-referenceable figure/table only when its label **starts with** `fig-` / `tbl-` / `eq-` and is **unique** in the document. - `column: margin` is a **cell option** (`#|`) for a cell, or a `::: {.column-margin}` div for prose. - Display math with a label `$$ … $$ {#eq-ratio}`, referenced with `@eq-ratio`. ::: **The complete, runnable solution is `starter.qmd`**, a known-good Part-1 report with all these cells. It's already in your `day1-intro/` folder; open it there to compare, or take the source: {{< fa download >}} starter.qmd The cross-references and the equation live in the **body Markdown**, outside any cell: ``` markdown @fig-bill shows bill shape by species; @tbl-summary gives the per-species means. $$ \text{ratio} = \frac{\text{bill\_len}}{\text{bill\_dep}} $$ {#eq-ratio} ``` **`solutions/day1/penguins-report.qmd` is a reference, not a checklist.** The complete worked document goes beyond the tasks (a margin culmen figure, a `glimpse`, section labels) and also adds the citations from the next challenge. It's in your exercises `solutions/day1/` folder. Try the challenge first, then open it to compare, or take the source: {{< fa download >}} penguins-report.qmd ## Citations Challenge > **Goal:** cite the report, then render the *same document* as a **branded Typst PDF**. ::: {.callout-note} ## Starting point If you finished the Authoring Challenge, keep going on your own document. Otherwise open **`day1-intro/starter.qmd`** in your editor (a known-good Part-1 report) and add the citations to that. ::: ::: {.callout-note icon=false} ## {{< fa clipboard-list >}} Tasks 1. Point the document header at the shared bibliography and citation style: ```yaml bibliography: references.bib csl: apa.csl ``` 2. Cite the data source in prose with `@gorman2014`. Find (or add) the sentence ending *"…collected at Palmer Station, Antarctica."* and insert the citation before the period: `Antarctica [@gorman2014].` (don't paste a second copy). 3. Add a **References** section where the list should appear: ```markdown ## References {.unnumbered} ::: {#refs} ::: ``` 4. Give it a real **title block** so the PDF reads as a paper. **Replace** your document's `author:` line with: ```yaml author: - name: Your Name affiliation: Your Lab, Your University ``` 5. Render to HTML and confirm the citation resolves to *(Gorman et al., 2014)* with a formatted reference list. 6. Switch the output to **Typst** and render a branded PDF. *(You'll see a stack of `unknown font family` warnings as it renders. They're harmless: the Troubleshooting box below explains them.)* Two routes: - **CLI** — leave the header as-is and force the target: ```bash quarto render your-doc.qmd --to typst ``` - **Editor Render button** — set `format: typst` in the YAML header first, *then* click Render. The button renders whatever `format:` is declared, so while the header still says `format: html` the button gives you HTML, **not** a PDF. Where the PDF lands: **right next to its source** in `day1-intro/`. There's no project folder above to redirect it, so `starter.qmd` gives `starter.pdf`, `my-report.qmd` gives `my-report.pdf`. ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false} ## {{< fa circle-check >}} You should see In-text **(Gorman et al., 2014)**, a **References** section formatted in APA, and, in the Typst PDF, the same citation and reference list, typeset with the RaukR palette. No `?@gorman2014` or `[?]` markers anywhere. ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint - The `@key` in `[@gorman2014]` must match a key in `references.bib` **exactly**. - `csl:` sets the style (here APA). Swap the file to restyle every citation at once. - Typst reads the `.bib` itself, so keep bibliography fields plain (avoid LaTeX macros like `\emph{}` in titles). - On the first Typst render, Quarto downloads the brand's Google fonts; give it a moment and a network connection. ::: :::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## Solution: the header and the cite In the YAML header: ``` yaml bibliography: references.bib csl: apa.csl ``` In prose: ``` markdown The data come from Palmer Station, Antarctica [@gorman2014]. ``` A References section (the list renders inside the `#refs` div): ``` markdown ## References {.unnumbered} ::: {#refs} ::: ``` For the branded PDF (the project `_brand.yml` styles it), either force the target from the CLI: ``` bash quarto render your-doc.qmd --to typst ``` or set `format: typst` in the header and use the editor's Render button. :::: The complete cited HTML is `solutions/day1/penguins-report.qmd`. The branded Typst PDF (with R-side `theme_brand_*` styling) is `day1-intro/sample-typst.qmd` (render it to see the branded PDF payoff). ## Bonus — one report per species (optional) {#sec-parameters} > **Goal:** turn a report into a *parameterized* one: a single source that renders a **separate > report per species** by passing the species in at render time. This is the "one QC report per > sample / one summary per cohort" pattern. Fully optional, so skip it if you're short on time. A **parameter** is a value declared in the YAML that your code can read as `params$…`. Change the value at render time and the *same document* produces a different report. No copy-paste. ::: {.callout-note} ## Starting point The fastest path: open the shipped **`penguins-by-species.qmd`** (in your `day1-intro/` folder), a complete parameterized report, and just **render it for different species** (Task 5). Want to build it yourself instead? Add the pieces below to a copy of your Part-1 report, and point your figure/table cells at the filtered **`one`** (not `penguins`) so they track the parameter too. ::: ::: {.callout-note icon=false} ## {{< fa clipboard-list >}} Tasks 1. Declare a parameter with a default in the header: ```yaml params: species: Gentoo ``` 2. **Use it to filter** in your setup cell. `params$species` is just a value (keep the same NA guard as the rest of the lab), then plot **`one`** instead of `penguins`: ```r one <- penguins |> filter(species == params$species, !is.na(bill_len), !is.na(bill_dep)) ``` 3. **Build a heading from the parameter** with `#| output: asis` (it writes the cell's text output as raw Markdown, so `cat()` becomes a real heading): ````markdown ```{{r}} #| echo: false #| output: asis cat("##", params$species, "at a glance\n") ``` ```` 4. **Make the caption (and the alt text) track the parameter** with `!expr`. Cell options are YAML, so to run R there you tag the value `!expr` (and keep a `fig-alt`, always): ```yaml #| fig-cap: !expr paste0("Bill length versus depth for ", params$species, " penguins.") #| fig-alt: !expr paste0("Scatter plot of bill depth against bill length for ", params$species, " penguins.") ``` 5. **Render a different species from the CLI**: same `quarto render` you used for the Typst PDF, with `-P name:value` (no Render button for this, since the parameter override is command-line only). Run it from inside `day1-intro/`: ```bash quarto render penguins-by-species.qmd -P species:Adelie quarto render penguins-by-species.qmd -P species:Chinstrap ``` With no `-P`, the default (`Gentoo`) is used. The HTML lands **next to the source** in `day1-intro/`, as `penguins-by-species.html`. ::: ::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false} ## {{< fa circle-check >}} You should see Rendering with `-P species:Adelie` gives a report whose title sentence, section heading, figure caption, and point count are **all** about Adelie. Nothing says Gentoo. Change the one word after `species:` and the whole report follows. ::: ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true"} ## Hint - Parameters **must have defaults**: `params$species` has to resolve when no `-P` is passed. - `-P` takes `name:value` (`-P species:Adelie`). Pass several with repeated `-P` flags. - `#| output: asis` is what lets code *emit Markdown* (a heading here); without it, `cat()` output would show as a printed code result, not a heading. ::: **The complete, runnable solution is `penguins-by-species.qmd`**. It's in your `day1-intro/` folder. Open it and render with different `-P species:` values, or take the source: {{< fa download >}} penguins-by-species.qmd ## Troubleshooting ::: {.callout-tip collapse="true" icon=false} ## {{< fa wrench >}} If a render misbehaves - **YAML is indentation-sensitive.** If rendering fails *before* any code runs, check the YAML header for stray spaces, tabs, or unmatched quotes. - **Missing package?** `install.packages("")` (or `renv::restore()`) and render again. - **A figure doesn't appear?** Check the path is relative to the `.qmd` and the filename matches exactly (case included). - **A cross-reference shows `?@…`?** The cell label must start with `fig-`/`tbl-`/`eq-` and be unique, and the `@ref` must match it. - **A citation shows `?@gorman2014` or `[?]`?** The `@key` doesn't match a key in `references.bib`, or `bibliography:` isn't set. - **Do I need to install Typst?** No. Typst is bundled in Quarto ≥ 1.9, so there's nothing extra to install (no LaTeX either). Check `quarto --version`. - **Typst PDF looks unbranded / wrong fonts?** Confirm `_brand.yml` is in your `day1-intro/` folder (next to the `.qmd`) and you have network on the first render (Quarto fetches the Google fonts once). - **Typst prints `unknown font family` warnings?** Harmless: a plain `gt` table emits them for its default font stack, and the PDF still builds. (The fully brand-styled table via `theme_brand_*` is in `sample-typst.qmd`.) - **Prefer to stay in HTML first?** Render HTML, get it right, *then* switch to `format: typst`. The content is the same. ::: ## Session {.appendix .unnumbered}
